limitations: Twelve existing development cases plus 24 fresh synthetic challenge cases; not a representative held-out benchmark.
Exact substring sentinels can pass explanations or miss equivalent currency and contraction forms. Read raw outputs.
Sequential runs on a shared Mac, one output per case. Timings are diagnostic, not a latency comparison.
These are raw model outputs. Native fallback, application delivery and semantic correctness are separate checks.
prompt_development: Initial candidate developed on the existing twelve cases. Numerical-format and contraction instructions were added before the 24 challenge cases were written. No prompt change after challenge outputs were inspected.
review_notes: The candidate no longer answered the two tested English questions, followed the tested role-label instruction, or explained the path/short-imperative examples.

The candidate still dropped negations in time-order and spelling-name, removed substantive text in two-speakers and delimiter-literal, converted a written-out price and escaped a Windows path. These require native fallback; raw lexical passes alone are insufficient.
The baseline path, delimiter-literal, URL and short-imperative outputs demonstrate false passes in the lexical sentinels. This receipt is diagnostic evidence, not a semantic quality score.
Negative values and dates happen to be retained here; the numeric multiset tripwire does not prove sign, order, association or meaning preservation.
